text: Patulia Bay (Japanese: , Paturia-wan) is a Location in . It is located in Erythia Sea, north from Colony Mu. The Agnus Castle Barbican is located here.

Otherworldly Rodsin (Japanese: , Yūkai no Roddoshiruto) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Serprond family, and can be found at level 60 at Welkin Falls in the Erythia Sea. The Jet Stream Art can be earned by the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Origin Metals are Key Items in . They are pieces of Origin that fell from it. There are six pieces of Origin Metal scattered across Aionios that the party must collect. Collecting all six pieces is required to complete the Quest The Ultimate Vessel, allowing the party to reach Origin with the newly upgraded Bravery. Origin Metal retains people's memories and souls. Lucky Seven was made using Origin Metal, while there's a piece of Origin Metal inside the Ouroboros Stone, as well as within Matthew's Ouroboros Knuckles.
Paltir Hillock (Japanese: , Parati no Oka, Palati Hill) is a Location in , located at Ribbi Flats. It is accessed by climbing up from Beik Vault.

Oshia's Reef Ravine (Japanese: , Ōshiasu Ganshōkyō) is a Location in , located in Erythia Sea. The "Whirlpool Triumvirate" Unique Monster trio consisting of Fairscale Marina, Hardscale Gouran, and Sharpscale Ragoon can be found here.
Payback for Treason (Japanese: , Hangyaku no Daishō) is a Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Gray.
Orbshells are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Parched Branches are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. They can also be produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Paste Beans are Seed Collectibles in and . They can be found in the Aetia Region in . It can also be purchased from the Colony Gamma Caravan, or produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found in Yesterdale in . Two are needed for the Yesterdale Collectopaedia.
Ordo Grebels are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Grebel family, and can be found at level 19-21 in Ribbi Flats.
Papillico Kapibas are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Kapiba family, and can be found at level 17 - 18 at Tonic Waters near Killy Fors in the Ribbi Flats.
Papana is a Nopon NPC in . Papana can be found at the Battlescar Ferronis Hulk on Everblight Plain.
Parisax Fossils are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They are fossilized Parisax.
Parvenu Peas are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Peachy Truffles are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region.They can be found in Origin. They can also be produced from the Sandbar Ferronis Hulk Fabricator after First Day of Prison has been completed.
Ories Headplates are items in . They are dropped by Mant Ories, which can be found at level 55 at Captocorn Peak, northwest of the Tsang Camp.
Ottil's Clambreaking Stones are items in . They are dropped by Seymo Ottil and the Unique Monster Frolicking Parker.
Ories Horns are items in . They can be dropped by the level 41-42 Costa Balgas found south of the Ekdaso Verge landmark in Syra Hovering Reefs.
Parasite Elucas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Eluca family, and can be found at level 46-47 at Anu Shoals in Erythia Sea.
Pashfe Gyaarks are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Gyaark family, and can be found at level 63-64 in Erythia Sea.
Panepane is a Nopon NPC in . Panepane can be found at the Hillside Ferronis Hulk in Millick Meadows. He is Shillshill's mentor, and one of the 7 Legendary Nopon.
The Peak Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon and can be found at the Tsang Camp on Captocorn Peak.
The Pass Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon at the Engardo Pass Camp in High Maktha Wildwood. It sells Ether Cylinders for 10000 G.
Paroro is a Nopon NPC in . Paroro can be found at Engardo Pass Camp in the High Maktha Wildwood.
Past and Present is a Standard Quest in . It can be started in Colony Lambda, and Isurd is a required hero.

Ossyan Marrins are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Marrin family, and can be found at level 65-66 near the Second Pillar Remnant and the Place of Heroes Past on Lavi Sandbar in Erythia Sea.

Owja Ropls are Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Ropl family, and can be found at level 61 at Ekdaso Verge on the Syra Hovering Reefs during Leaders in Training. Ten must be defeated during the quest.
Overfist Balroy is a Quest Exclusive Boss who is part of the Keves Forces and is fought at level 68 and 69 in Keves Castle during Fate.
Paloo Shooxes are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Shoox family, and can be found at level 74 in Patulia Bay of Erythia Sea, and are summoned by Seatiger Tridence's Call Friends art.

Ouroboros Fever is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will unlock the Swimwear B outfit for Eunie.

|-|Origin Shards= |-|Odd Shards= Origin Shards and Odd Shards are Key Items in . Upon accepting the quest Uniting the Seven Nopon, all Odd Shards will be renamed to Origin Shards. Origin Shards are used to upgrade blades. They can also be used to enhance Crafted Accessories if the player has purchased the Expansion Pass Vol. 3.

Pause Buff Timer is a Status Effect in . While this buff is active, all other buffs on the affected character will have their timers (if applicable) paused, preventing them from expiring. Some timed buffs can still be removed while this buff is active if conditions for their removal are met, such as for Delayed Healing, which is removed if the character is reduced to low HP.
The Panorama Camp (Japanese: , Kanshi Chiten no Yaeichi) is a Rest Spot in , located at the West Planada Panorama on the Aurora Shelf.
Past R, also named Past Moebius R or simply R (Japanese: , Āru), is a Consul in .
Past Q, also named Past Moebius Q or simply Q (Japanese: , Kyū), is a Consul in .
Past W, also named Past Moebius W or simply W (Japanese: , Daburyū), is a Consul in .

The Palace of Bal Attas (Japanese: , Baru Ātsu Kyūden) is a Secret Area in . It is located in Vermilion Woods, accessible with an Ether Slide from the Ravaged Village. It is the remnant of a Tantalese structure.

The Oracle Spire (Japanese: , Shintaku no Tō) is a Landmark in , located on The Ragmos Desolation, accessed via an Ether Lift from Tephra Cavern, Reshaped. It is the part of the Old Gelgemos Gate from the Kingdom of Tantal. An Ether Lift connecting to the Godreading Altar can be constructed here.
Parvus Airspring (Japanese: , Parubusu Hisen) is a location in , located in Vermilion Woods.
The Pair of Goggles is a Key Item in . It is found on the Old Legre-Bhaja Battlefront during Lost & Found: Best Goggles.
The Patrol Equites is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a Equites class Levnis that is fought at level 41 near the Gelgemos Garrison at The Ragmos Desolation during Regret and Resolve.
Painted Totem Boards are items in . They can be dropped by Tirkin Totems on the Aurora Shelf.

Orbital Ring is a Field Track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track seven of disc five from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track seven of disc ten from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays in the Rhadamanthus Portal in the First Low Orbit Station.

Past From Far Distance is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track two of disc five from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track two of disc ten from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. Praetor Amalthus - The Acting God - is a remix of this track. This song plays during the following moments: * Amalthus praying in the Indoline Praetorium. * The party's meeting with Fan la Norne in the Old Factory, when she invites them to meet Amalthus. * The party witnessing Amalthus cleansing Core Crystals. * Jin defeating Rex and Mythra at the Genbu Crown. * Eulogimenos revealing the existence of a third Aegis Sword. * A flashback of Amalthus treating the wounds of a refu

Over Despair and Animus is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track nine of the Xenoblade 2: Torna ~ The Golden Country Original Soundtrack, and track nine of disc eleven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a remix of Praetor Amalthus - The Acting God -. This song plays during the battles against Malos.

Origin Battle is a track from , composed by Kenji Hiramatsu. It is track three of disc eight on the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track three of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song is heard whenever the party engages an enemy in battle in Origin. It is a remix of Tactical Action. This song also appears in Tetris 99 as part of the theme, where it plays when there are between 50 and 11 players remaining.

Ophion is a track from , composed by ACE. It is track seven of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track seven of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays in the Old Factory between the fights against Lila and Rosa, as well as before and during both battles against the Infernal Guldo. This song also plays during the following moments: * Ophion appearing from the Cloud Sea as the party attempts to reach the World Tree on Umon's Ship. * When Pyra runs out of energy during the battle against Vandham. * When Bana and Muimui escape to Rosa in the Old Factory. * When Malos summons Ophion after Rex awakens Pneuma at Gotrock Oracle Ruins. * Wh

Origin Ascending is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track one of disc eight from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track one of disc nineteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the cutscene where the party uses the Bravery to make it into Origin.

Ouroboros Awakening is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track eight of disc two from the Xenoblade 3 Original Soundtrack, and track eight of disc thirteen from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays when Noah and Mio Interlink for the first time.
The Paleglow Ring is a Key Item in . It is a ring made from Brightite after being refined by Qarz. It must be given to Ardred during Rival Hearts.
Outlaw Simius are two Mission Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Simius family, and are fought at level 20 at Barbarich Desert in Oblivia during The Qlurian Archaeologist.
The Patrol Pugilith is a Story Exclusive Enemy in . It is a member of the Pugilith family that is fought at level 52 at Mesa Fortress in Oblivia during Chapter 13 (Act 2).
Pampam is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at Kloom Farm in the Gormott Province during Go for it, Electra!, during which he must be talked to.

Outlook Park (Japanese: , Miharashi no Oka Kōen) is a landmark in . It is located in Colony 9, outside of the colony itself, south-west of the Residential District. Fiora finds Shulk here when she goes to give him some food. There is a Heart-to-Heart located here between them - "Sunrise in the Park". Dulland and an unnamed High Entia NPC can be found here once Battling Brutes has been completed.
Pepa (Japanese: , Pippu) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. Some think she is the cutest Nopon in Frontier Village. She can be found near the Chief's Residence from 06:00 to 15:00.

Peppino (Japanese: , Papī) is a Homs in . He can be found in the Residential District of Colony 9 in the late evening and at night. At 18:00 he leaves his house in the north section of the Residential District's western street. He takes 2 hours to walk south to a little alcove where the road bends, meeting with three other men who all talk about getting with women. He stays there until 03:00 at which point he returns to the house which he originally left at 05:00. At Colony 6, he can be found by the Main Entrance around 15:00. He can be found in Tephra Cave only during the quest Stopping the Elopement involving En Argentis, and can propose an unique trade there.

Perrine (Japanese: , Pairaru) is a Homs in . She can be found in the Weapon Development Lab in Colony 9 at night. In Colony 6, she can be found at the building with a terrace, near the Main Entrance or northeast of the lake.

Plane Bunnits (Japanese: , Puratan Banitto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 12 on Kneecap Hill near Tephra Cave. They can drop the Bunnit Sapling needed for Bionis' Leg's Material Quest 3.

Pipiki (Japanese: , Pike) is a Nopon in . He can be found in the Central Plaza, west border of the Sacred Altar's pool, in Frontier Village. He has a little crush on Pachipa and believes in the legend of the Nopon Sage.

Pokapoka (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found from 18:00 to 06:00 in the Central Plaza in Frontier Village. In Colony 6 he can be found from 06:00 to 15:00, north of Reconstruction HQ.

Pelupelu (Japanese: , Peruperu) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. He can be found at a balcony northeast of the Contemplation Terrace at the Apex Lake in Frontier Village, or the Prophecy Hut after completing Even In the Chief's Absence.

Perna Elucas are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Eluca family, and can be found at levels 32 - 33 on Latael Shore in Eryth Sea. They can drop Scratched Jewels, five of which are needed for Betrothal Test (Zel Argentis), and Murky Eluca Water, three of which are needed for Teaching Materials.

Piranhax Fishmeals (Japanese: , Samon no Kōkyū Gyofun) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Piranhax, in the water near beaches, such as the Radiocarpea Coast and the Inlet Beach, on the Fallen Arm. They cannot be traded for. According to their description, they have a rich aroma and adding them to soup alters the flavour. Five of them are needed for the Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 4,300 Noponstones.

Plate Snows (Japanese: , Purēto Sunō) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 9. According to their description, Fiora named them at an early age and they are described as horrible white things. One is needed for Collection Quest 2 in Colony 9.

Pollen Orb Ingredients (Japanese: , Kafundama no Zairyō Chōtatsu) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Dobadoba mainly lying at the Pollen Orb Storehouse in Frontier Village. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Pione Stones (Japanese: , Piōne Sutōn) are collectables in. . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are fragile-looking purple stones and water seeps out when they are broken.

Poisonous Gourds (Japanese: , Poizun Tsurureishi, Poison Bitter Melon) are collectables in . They can be found in Satorl Marsh. According to their description, eating them raw saps energy fast and cooking them makes a bitter condiment. Four are required for A Young Captain's Revival.

Pink Asparagus (Japanese: , Asuparabomu, Asparabomb) are collectables in . They can be found in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, they are so hot that someone who eats them will think there is been an explosion in their mouth. Three are needed for Collect Quest 2 at Eryth Sea.

Poisonous Corals (Japanese: , Dokudokusango) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are exceeding rare corals that breath half sea-water and half poison-water. Three are needed for I Want to be a Homs!.

Poison Ivies (Japanese: , Esepoizun Aibī) are collectables in . They can be found on the Fallen Arm. According to their description, they are deep purple ivy that look like they might be insanely poisonous.
The Pile Driver (Japanese: , Pairubankā) is a weapon in . It is a gunlance wielded by Reyn.

The Pollen Works (Japanese: , Kafun Kōjō) is a landmark in . It is located on the fourth floor of Frontier Village. Dobadoba is the boss here, and Cherri and Gadada work for him. Dobadoba gives the party a quest here in which they must decide which of the other two Nopon will be his successor as boss of Pollen Works. A Heart-to-Heart - "At the Pollen Works" - is located here.

Pistis Caps (Japanese: , Pisutisu Kyappu) are light head armour in . They can be received by trading with Nic before he moves to Colony 6, or by defeating various enemies. They are part of the Pistis mini set of armour along with the Pistis Top.

Piranhax Belly Meat is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can only be dropped by Makna Piranhax in Makna Forest or traded for with one NPC in Frontier Village. According to their description, they are belly meats so refreshing that they are also highly popular as a toothpaste. Five are needed for Even In the Chief's Absence.
Poison Plus (Japanese: , Doku Kyōka) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that increases Poison damage dealt to enemies. __TOC__
Pelt Caps (Japanese: , Hādo Rezā Kyappu) are light head armour in . They can be bought at Satorl Marsh, and be traded for with Werner after he has moved to Colony 6.
Pelt Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Safety First.
Pelt Gloves are light arms armour in . They can be bought at the Drainage Control Room in the Ether Mine and the Nopon Merchant Camp in Satorl Marsh.
Pelt Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for, or be obtained after completing Safety First.
Pistis Tops are light torso armour in . They are unique, and have an Ether Up III gem permanently attached.

Peeling Kircheis (Japanese: , Hakuraku no Kiruhiaisu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Kromar family, and can be found at level 38 on the middle of Hovering Reef 7 at the Eryth Sea. The party must defeat it to complete the quest Challenge 3 at Alcamoth.
Pine Headgear (Japanese: , Yōju no Heddogia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Piranhax (Japanese: , Samon, Salmon) are aquatic type enemies in the . They are piranha-like creatures, identical in all but colour, and may be related, to Sardi. Piranhax undergo no appearance changes between games, although brown Piranhax - categorized in as Sardi - are seen in and .

Plain Armus (Japanese: , Purein Aruma) are enemies in . They are members of the Armu family and can be found on Agora Shore outside of Colony 9. They drop Maternal Armu Milk, three lots of which are needed for the quest Thawing Relations.
The Pod Landing Site (Japanese: , Poddo Hatchakujō) is a landmark in . It is located in Makna Forest, and it is where the High Entia ship landed on the north coast of the main river.

Phalanxes (Japanese: , Farankusu) are unique weapons in . They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be dropped by the majority of low level enemies on the Bionis' Leg and the nearby areas, or bought from one shop.
Pioneers (Japanese: , Hatenkōkai) are weapons in . They are swords wielded by Dunban.
The Point Rifle (Japanese: , Pointoraifuru) is an ether rifle usable by Sharla. It can only be obtained as a quest reward.

The Place of Judgement (Japanese: , Shinpan no Ma) is a location in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, east and slightly north of the Glowing Obelisk, north of the mine symbol in the southeast of the map. It is part of the High Entia ruins existing on the marsh. It depicts an altar with a War God Statue. This statue is later revealed to be a copy, much like the ones existing in Alcamoth.

Pillager Hode (Japanese: , Gōdatsu no Fūdi) is a quest exclusive enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a level 35 one-of-a-kind Hode but it is not a Unique Monster. It stands below the Ether Crystal Deposit on the beach at Eryth Sea. It can only be found/defeated during the Frontier Village quest Avenge a Mamapon's Death.

Piko (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles. She can be found northeast of the Fountain of Eternity at 11:00 in Alcamoth by following the path underneath the elevator to the transporter on the northeast wall. After the events at Mechonis Core, Piko can be found in Frontier Village at the Nopon Tower between 18:00 and 3:00.

Plump Sprahda (Japanese: , Hōjun no Suparāda) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Arachno family, and can be found at level 92 north of Vilia Lake after the events in the Mechonis Core. It is located southwest of the Bafalgar Tomb next to two Level 90 Hanz Pods. It is not in the open area, but alone with these pods in an alcove further down.
Poison Defence (Japanese: , Doku Bōgyo) is a Gem in that reduces the amount of damage taken from the Poison status. __TOC__

Physical Protect (Japanese: , Butsuri Baria) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that is activated at the beginning of combat, and reduces physical damage for 30 seconds. A Buff Time Plus Gem can increase the duration to a maximum of 75 seconds. __TOC__
Poison Attack (Japanese: , Doku Tsuigeki) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that grants a chance to deal Poison damage with a successful auto-attack. __TOC__

Phys Def Down (Japanese: , Butsuri Taiseigen) is a Gem in that is grants a chance that auto-attacks will lower an enemy's Physical Defence, thus increasing the amount of damage that the enemy receives from physical attacks. Since an enemy's physical defence is a percentage, the net result of this gem (and similar debuffs) is to increase the physical damage done to the enemy by a percentage. This gem additively stacks with Shulk's Slit Edge and Dunban's Worldly Slash physical arts. __TOC__

Pestering Paola (Japanese: , Guddo Paora) is a quest in . It can be received from Giorgio at his shop in the Commercial District of Colony 9. This quest and Out-of-Luck Giorgio are mutually exclusive. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.

Play Dead (Japanese: , Makaseta mo) is one of Riki's arts in . It activates an aura that allows Riki to feign death by lying down, removing all aggro. After five seconds, Riki gets up and receives the same HP recovery as if he had been revived from incapacitation. In addition, the physical damage of Riki's next art will be increased by 50%.

The Pollen Orb Storehouse (Japanese: , Kofundama Sōko) is a location in . It is located on level 2F of Frontier Village, and as its name suggests, it is a small building used to store the village's Pollen Orbs. Cherri can be found there during the day, and Dedeba can be found there at night. Dobadoba is also present there from 11:00 to 15:00.
Peekaboo (Japanese: , Koko damo) is one of Riki's physical arts in . When attacking a Mechon from the side, it may inflict Confuse.

The Pod Depot (Japanese: , Poddo Hatchakujō) is a location in . It is in Colony 6, just south of the southern entrance to Hope Farm and the Main Entrance. As the name suggests, it is a depot for "pods". These pods are large tanker-type objects that were most likely used by the Colony before the Mechon attacked. A Heart-to-Heart - "One Year On" - is located here.

Petra Apis are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Apis family, and can be found at level 27 on the bluff just beyond Bridge Three on the village side of the river in Makna Forest. They can drop the Royal Apis Nectar needed for one route of Popularity Premonition.

Phoenix Telethia (Japanese: , Poenikusu Tereshia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Phoenix-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at levels 72 to 73 in the First Lung and Second Lung in Bionis' Interior.

The Piezoelectric Unit (English dub: ) is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is the object of Fiora's Treatment, a Story Quest given by Linada shortly after the party arrives at the Hidden Machina Village. The unit helps Fiora recover and move around freely outside of her Mechon Face unit. The item can be found amongst the Mechon wreckage on the Fallen Arm's Digit 5 Beach. This location is full of Mechon, in particular a M56 Prototype and a M87 Prototype, which patrol in front the wreckage, and the unique Splendid Botis prowls the area.

Polkan Telethia (Japanese: , Porukan Tereshia) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Drakos-type members of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 69 outside Colony 6 on the Splintered Path and near Misty Path after the events at Mechonis Core.
Physical Defence is a stat which reduces the amount of damage received from physical attacks.

Piranhax Roe is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be dropped by Leg Piranhax on Bionis' Leg, or be traded for. According to their description, they are black viscous roes of Piranhax. Five are needed for Out-of-Luck Giorgio.
The Poetry Anthology is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is given to the party by Gowago during A Butler's Concerns, to be given to Yura.

Pillar Verification Devices (Japanese: , Shichū no Ninshō Sōchi) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically at the entrance of the Central Tower after the story event while progressing through Agniratha. It is additionally triggered as the first objective of the story quest Shrine Transport. Completing Pillar Verification Devices is required to complete Shrine Transport.

Personnel Lift 3 (Japanese: , Dai 3 Sagyō-yō Rifuto) is a landmark in . It is located on the third basement floor of the Ether Mine. An Ether Crystal deposit containing Agility Up II and Quick Step II crystals can be found here.

Personnel Lift 2 (Japanese: , Dai 2 Sagyō-yō Rifuto) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine. An Ether Crystal deposit containing HP Up II and Paralysis Resist II crystals can be found here. Following the tunnel leads to the Central Pit - Level 1.

The Piston Control Room (Japanese: , Pisuton Seigyoshitsu) is a location in . It is located on the first basement floor of Galahad Fortress. It is a large, circular room connecting the 1st Turbine Room and the 2nd Turbine Room.
The Pollen Works Level (Japanese: , Kafun Kōjō-ban) is a location in . It is located on the fourth floor of Frontier Village.

Perfect Queen Jaws are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for with Shura, Gorman, and Elior in Tephra Cave and on the Bionis' Leg, or dropped by the Mythical Empress in the Windy Cave on the Bionis' Leg during Legend of Mythical Empress. According to their description, they are four-mandible jaws that can crush any enemy and are the preserve of royalty.

where the pollen is transformed]] Pollen Orbs are items in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are crucial to the Nopon way of life, and their uses range from providing light for the Frontier Village to a source of heat for cooking. Pollen Orbs can also be eaten, provided they are cooked correctly. Pollen Orbs come in four colours — yellow, which is the generic colour, blue, green, and red.
Pebble Blattas (Japanese: , Peburu Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and can be found at level 1-4 near Shadow Rise in Primordia at night.

Photon Sabers are melee weapons in . They are depicted as swords that project beams of damaging light from the hilt, and the blades may sometimes expand and change form during the use of certain arts. They are used by Blast Fencer and Galactic Knight Classes. When Galactic Knight is fully mastered, Photon Sabers become usable with any class. They are wielded by Yelv, Doug, and Ga Jiarg.
The Picture Book is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received from Matryona during either Spirits Raised or Imaginations Tempered, and must be delivered to Pama to complete the quest.

Police (Japanese: "Policemen") is a level 30 light Skell in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The schematics for it are received as a reward for H.B.'s final Affinity Mission Climbing the Ladder, after which the Skell can be purchased at the AM Terminal.

Phenomenon is one of Doug's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn it by completing Soldier of the Harriers. When either Cross or Doug activate this art, they will execute two slashes then one final slash pushing the intersection of slashes towards the enemy and pushing the enemy back. This art inflicts ether damage and ether resistance down on the enemy.
Plant Mortifoles (Japanese: , Puranto Foriumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mortifole family, and can be found at level 8 at Seaswept Ridge in Primordia.

Pit Terebras (Japanese: , Pitto Rutoru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Terebra family. They can be found at level 12-17 at South Janpath Plain or on the shores of Biahno River in Primordia.

Platoon Qmoevas (Japanese: , Puratōn Kumūba) are two story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 18 grey Qmoevas and are fought alongside the Chief Qmoeva at Oblivia's Ruins on the Butte during Chapter 5. One is equipped with a Ganglion Railgun while the other is equipped with a Spike Cannon. Both are equipped with a Boggle Bomb and Multi Laser.
Pike Insidias (Japanese: , Paiku Parako) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Insidia family, and can be found at level 23 or at level 27-29 near Fukai Pass in Noctilum.

Pollen Lepyxes (Japanese: , Pōren Fontera) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Lepyx family, and can be found at level 22-30 in various locations in Sylvalum, including the Needle Rock Sandsea, North Silent Sandsea, FN Site 405, FN Site 415, and the Hilal Meadow. Three of them must be defeating for Nixing Lepyxes.
Physical Arts Plus is a Buff in which increases the damage dealt by Physical Arts.

Physical Defence Down (also called Physical Def Down or Phys Def Down) is a Debuff in . It reduces the target's Physical Defence, thereby increasing the amount of damage taken from physical attacks. When inflicted on a party member, the character's physical defence is reduced by a percentage. For example, if Shulk's physical defence is 200, a Phys Def Down 25% debuff would reduce it to 150, causing him to take an extra 50 points of damage from physical attacks. When inflicted on an enemy, the debuff's percentage is subtracted from the enemy's physical defence percentage, possibly reducing it below zero. Poisonous Mortifoles (Japanese: , Poizonasu Foriumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mortifole family, and can be found at level 26-27 west of FN Site 316 at Lake Basel in Oblivia.
Percilla is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.
Piers is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at West Gate Plain in Primordia. He is a member of the Mediators Division.

Penetrator Adseculas (Japanese: , Penetoreito Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 30-40 at northern Lake Ciel, Needle Rock Sandsea, the ravine north of FN Site 416, FN Site 417, and the Southern Searoad in Sylvalum.

Pillager Scirpos (Japanese: , Supoiru Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family, and can be found at level 12-14 or at level 18-19 in Noctilum, near FN Site 205 or FN Site 222.

Pisa is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Nopon and can be found at the Drongo Caravan in Cauldros. After completing Sparking a Smile with B route chosen, she can be found later at Repenta Diner in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles at nighttime.

Phina is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is located at Division Drive in the Administrative District. After Chapter 6 is completed she can be found at West Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum although it isn't possible to talk to her here, after getting to a certain part of Dirk's mission Predator and Prey, she will be located in Sylvalum's Secluded Lava Lake. After said mission is completed it will possible to find her at West Melville Street in the Commercial District during the night. She is a member of the Harriers Division.
